If the individual encounters the actual pathogen in the future, their immune system can quickly recognize and neutralize it, preventing illness or reducing its severity.

When enough people are immune, it becomes challenging for the disease to spread, as there are fewer susceptible individuals for the pathogen to infect. This indirectly protects individuals who are not immune, such as those who cannot be vaccinated due to medical reasons.
